snapshots.caption: During accepted RDE job, shortly after telemetry reached layer 1/696. Black filament on the textured plate is difficult to distinguish in this wide view; adhesion and finished quality are not certified.
During exact accepted job6370, around layer43/696. Visible deposited parts and toolhead; this frame does not establish cleanup, dimensions, strength or operation.
During AMS-overload pause at81%; parts remain on bed. This frame does not prove the filament path or physical quality.
After the authorized AMS resume; same job advanced beyond layer497. Parts remain on bed; no physical acceptance claimed.
After the owner removed the parts. The bed is empty; this does not show finished-part quality. The printer was still paused at the final layer with a filament-retraction fault.

source.evidence: Current main online gate, local guide synchronization and exact retained-mesh slice audit passed. M4 upload and download were identical; printer acknowledged exact file, MD5, plate 1 and AMS A3. Start sent once; PREPARE, RUNNING and layer 1 observed.

notes: First specimen of each selected part; no old-design stock credit. Slicer 02.08.02.61: 0.15 mm layers (0.20 first), 3 walls, 15% infill, 5 mm outer brims, 220 C nozzle / 55 C textured PEI. Both preview fields intentionally reference the actual first-layer GCode plot. Native 3MF PNG thumbnails are absent: headless rendering returned no bitmap. Cleanup, dimensions, strength and operation remain unverified. Actual time and filament are unmeasured. Start timestamp is observed acceptance, not first extrusion. Geometry: HdM Project ENIGMA R.D.E., Prof. Dr. Simon Wiest, revision 397ca89, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. On17November, observed PAUSE at81%, layer497/696 with AMS assist-motor overload (print_error117473296); actual pause onset is unknown. One owner-authorized AMS RESUME was sent at13:37:05UTC. Fresh telemetry at13:39:06UTC verified the same task6370 RUNNING, layer498,82%, print_error0; later layer502 observed. Same attempt continued, not a new print. Completion, actual duration/usage and physical quality remain unverified. On 17 November at 16:37 UTC, fresh telemetry reported PAUSE at 99%, layer 696/696, zero estimated minutes remaining and a filament-retraction fault. The owner had already removed the parts and requested the next print. The controller sent one stop command; the printer then reported FAILED with task-cancelled error. This is recorded as cancelled, not a verified successful completion. Final-layer deposition, cleanup, strength and fit remain unverified. Exact terminal timestamp and active printing duration are not established.
